quoted_tweet.author: Serenity
quoted_tweet.text:
Goldman Sachs in their recent note upgraded their global optical module market forecast to:  

- $67.7 billion (+33% revision) for 2026
- $131.4 billion (+81% revision) for 2027
- $148.5 billion (+115% revision) for 2028

For $NVDA Rubin Ultra, GS increased its modeled optical modules per GPU:

1.6T: 0 -> 2
3.2T: 3 -> 5 

GS also raised their 1.6T and above forecast for 2027 by 61%... so that's also very material, with 80% silicon photonics penetration rate estimated. 

So more optical content per chip = a lot more CW lasers, more SOI substrates, happy optical companies.

OpenAI published its own guide to prompting GPT-6 Astra.

Most people are still using it like GPT-5. That’s the problem.

1. Audit your AGENTS.​md and skill files → old instructions now get in the way

2. Tell it to bias toward action → otherwise Astra stops to ask instead of continuing

3. Don’t tell it to run tests → it already does, and repeating it causes overtesting

4. Say when to use subagents → it won't split up the work unless you tell it to

5. Set the writing style → it defaults to long, formatted answers with repeated phrases

Astra works best when you set the goal and let it own the work.

Bookmark this before your next build.

The doc explains Astra. This guide shows you how to brief it for free:

https://godofprompt.ai/guides/gpt6-astra-mastery-guide

The rest of the library is at https://godofprompt.ai

Follow if you'd rather rewrite 5 lines in your prompt than fight the model on every run.
